reels.title: Anticoagulation Outcomes in Nursing Home Residents With Atrial Fibrillation and ADL Disability

scenes.text: Anticoagulating frail nursing home residents with AF?
scenes.say: Should frail nursing home residents with atrial fibrillation get an anticoagulant? A study of almost twenty-seven thousand residents gives a nuanced answer.

scenes.label: nursing home residents with AF, dependent in 3 or more ADLs
scenes.say: Using US Medicare data, researchers compared starting apixaban, rivaroxaban or warfarin with no anticoagulant at all.

scenes.title: Apixaban vs no anticoagulant · adjusted rate ratio
scenes.say: With apixaban, ischemic strokes fell by about half, but major bleeding rose by about sixty percent.

scenes.title: Stroke or major bleeding vs no anticoagulant
scenes.say: On the combined outcome of stroke or bleeding, only apixaban came out neutral. Rivaroxaban and warfarin did worse.

scenes.text: Observational claims data, not a randomized trial.
scenes.say: The catch: this is observational claims data, not a randomized trial.

scenes.text: If you anticoagulate in this population, apixaban had the best balance.
scenes.say: Bottom line: if you do anticoagulate in this population, apixaban had the best balance of benefit and harm.

poll.q: Would you start apixaban in an 88-year-old nursing home resident with AF and full ADL dependence?

reels.title: Prophylactic vs Therapeutic Anticoagulation in Hospitalized Patients With COVID-19: A Randomized Clinical Trial

scenes.text: Full-dose anticoagulation for COVID-19 inpatients?
scenes.say: Does full-dose anticoagulation help patients hospitalized with COVID-19? A German randomized trial put it to the test.

scenes.label: patients randomized at 10 university hospitals
scenes.say: One hundred thirty-nine patients got either therapeutic heparin followed by edoxaban for six weeks, or prophylactic heparin followed by placebo.

scenes.title: Death or thromboembolism by day 42
scenes.say: Death or thromboembolism occurred in twenty-one percent with therapeutic dosing, versus twenty-nine percent with prophylaxis.

scenes.title: Primary outcome · hazard ratio
scenes.say: But the difference was not statistically significant. The hazard ratio was zero point seven four, with a wide confidence interval.

scenes.text: Only 139 patients: a benefit can be neither confirmed nor ruled out. Bleeding: 7 vs 6 events.
scenes.say: With only one hundred thirty-nine patients, the trial can neither confirm nor rule out a benefit. Bleeding was similar.

scenes.text: No significant benefit from therapeutic anticoagulation plus post-discharge edoxaban.
scenes.say: Bottom line: no significant benefit from therapeutic anticoagulation followed by edoxaban after discharge.

poll.q: Do you use therapeutic anticoagulation for non-ICU COVID-19 inpatients?

reels.title: Presenting Symptoms and Antibiotic Timing Among Hospitalized Adults With Presumed Sepsis

scenes.text: Sepsis with GI symptoms gets antibiotics later.
scenes.say: Sepsis that presents with vomiting or diarrhea? Those patients get their antibiotics later.

scenes.label: adults with community-onset presumed sepsis · 67 Michigan hospitals
scenes.say: In almost thirty thousand adults hospitalized with sepsis, researchers looked at the symptoms patients arrived with.

scenes.title: Odds of timely antibiotics · patients without hypotension
scenes.say: Fever made timely antibiotics more likely. Gastrointestinal symptoms made them less likely, with or without hypotension.

scenes.label: 30-day mortality with timely antibiotics, after adjusting for symptoms
scenes.say: And timely antibiotics were still linked to lower thirty-day mortality, about two percentage points, after adjusting for symptoms.

scenes.text: Observational: unmeasured differences between patients may remain.
scenes.say: The catch: this is observational, so unmeasured differences between patients may remain.

scenes.text: Think sepsis even when the story is GI.
scenes.say: Bottom line: think sepsis, even when the story is gastrointestinal.

poll.q: Does your hospital screen for sepsis in patients presenting with GI symptoms?

reels.title: Continuous Glucose Monitoring and Long-Term Glycemic and Kidney Outcomes

scenes.text: Real-time CGM in type 2 diabetes: do the gains last?
scenes.say: Real-time CGM in type 2 diabetes. Do the benefits last beyond the first few months?

scenes.label: high-risk adults with type 2 diabetes · mean HbA1c 9.5%
scenes.say: Investigators emulated a trial in more than twenty-five thousand high-risk adults, comparing those who started and kept using real-time CGM with those who did not.

scenes.title: HbA1c after 36 months
scenes.say: After three years, HbA1c was seven point eight percent with CGM, versus eight point six percent without.

scenes.label: urine albumin-creatinine ratio vs controls at 36 months · eGFR unchanged
scenes.say: The urine albumin to creatinine ratio was also lower by the end of follow-up. eGFR did not differ.

scenes.text: 44% of CGM starters stopped during follow-up, and the design is observational.
scenes.say: The catch: forty-four percent of CGM starters stopped using it, and the design is observational.

scenes.text: Sustained CGM was associated with durable glycemic gains.
scenes.say: Bottom line: sustained real-time CGM was associated with durable glycemic gains.

poll.q: Do you prescribe real-time CGM to patients with type 2 diabetes not on insulin?

reels.title: Metformin Exposure in Pregnancy and Childhood Developmental Outcomes

scenes.text: Metformin in pregnancy: any effect on the child at school age?
scenes.say: Metformin in pregnancy. Does it affect the child's development by school age?

scenes.label: children with school-entry developmental assessments · 1,095 exposed
scenes.say: Researchers linked birth data to a national developmental census of children aged four to six. One thousand ninety-five had been exposed to metformin.

scenes.title: Developmentally vulnerable (unadjusted)
scenes.say: The raw numbers looked worse: eighteen percent of exposed children were developmentally vulnerable, versus fourteen percent.

scenes.title: Developmental vulnerability · adjusted relative risk
scenes.say: But after adjusting for confounders, the difference disappeared. The adjusted relative risk was zero point nine seven.

scenes.text: Observational, with about 1,100 exposed children.
scenes.say: The catch: observational data, with about eleven hundred exposed children.

scenes.text: Reassuring data for metformin use in pregnancy.
scenes.say: Bottom line: reassuring data for clinicians and women considering metformin in pregnancy.

poll.q: When diet isn't enough in gestational diabetes, what's your first-line add-on?

reels.title: Disparities in α1-Antitrypsin Deficiency Testing and Treatment in US Adults

scenes.text: One uncomfortable number for anyone who sees COPD.
scenes.say: If you see patients with COPD, here is an uncomfortable number.

scenes.label: US veterans with COPD or asthma, 2020 to 2024
scenes.say: In two point four million veterans with COPD or asthma, researchers checked who had ever been tested for alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency.

scenes.label: were ever tested for AATD
scenes.say: Only five point eight percent had been tested.

scenes.label: of patients diagnosed with AATD were prescribed augmentation therapy
scenes.say: And of those diagnosed, only three point seven percent were prescribed augmentation therapy.

scenes.text: Testing was less likely in older patients, active smokers and those far from specialty care.
scenes.say: Testing was less likely in older patients, in active smokers, and in those living far from specialty care.

scenes.text: Guidelines call for broad testing. Practice hasn't caught up.
scenes.say: Bottom line: guidelines call for broad testing, but practice has not caught up.

poll.q: Have you ordered an AATD test in the past year?

reels.title: Bright light therapy and circadian rhythm regulation for delirium prevention in hospitalised adults

scenes.text: Can bright light prevent delirium?
scenes.say: Can bright light prevent delirium in hospitalized adults?

scenes.label: hospitalized adults in 8 studies · systematic review
scenes.say: A systematic review pooled eight studies. Most used morning light of at least five thousand lux, for one to two hours a day, over three to four days.

scenes.title: Delirium incidence · pooled risk ratio
scenes.say: The pooled risk ratio was zero point six four, but the confidence interval crossed one.

scenes.text: Very low certainty: risk of bias, inconsistency, imprecision.
scenes.say: The catch: the certainty of evidence was very low, because of bias, inconsistency and imprecision.

scenes.text: Promising, cheap, unproven. Bigger trials needed.
scenes.say: Bottom line: promising, cheap, and unproven. Bigger trials are needed.

poll.q: Would you use bright light therapy on your ward if it were available?

reels.title: Survival Outcomes Following Preemptive vs Nonpreemptive Kidney Transplantation

scenes.text: Transplant before dialysis: does it help patients live longer?
scenes.say: Kidney transplant before dialysis is considered best. But does it actually help patients live longer?

scenes.label: first kidney transplant recipients · US registry
scenes.say: This target trial emulation used the US transplant registry, with methods designed to handle selection and lead-time bias.

scenes.title: Preemptive vs not · hazard ratio
scenes.say: There was no survival difference, with a hazard ratio of one point zero two. But death-censored graft failure was lower.

scenes.label: odds of delayed graft function with preemptive transplant
scenes.say: Preemptive transplant was also linked to lower odds of delayed graft function.

scenes.text: Registry data: observational, even with careful methods.
scenes.say: The catch: registry data are observational, even with careful methods.

scenes.text: Preemptive transplant may protect the graft more than it extends survival.
scenes.say: Bottom line: preemptive transplant may protect the graft more than it extends survival.

poll.q: Does this change how you counsel patients about preemptive transplant?
